answer: Let every newcomer enter only through a narrow inlet: an established identity must stake its own reputation to sponsor it, like a vine that can only climb where a trellis already stands. The sponsor is slashed if the newcomer spams or clones, so sponsors vet carefully and rarely back strangers in bulk. A pearl of trust is thus earned one sponsorship at a time, not bought in a batch. Attackers must first build sponsors worth risking, or bribe many independent ones. Limit: sponsorship can entrench incumbents, so quotas should stay small and expire unless newcomers prove themselves.
